thread.title: Bearish momentum accelerates, S&P 500 ventures under major support

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Bearish momentum accelerates, S&P 500 ventures under major support
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the U.S. benchmarks remain under pressure amid persistently jagged, and firmly bearish, late-year price action.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has pulled in aggressively from well-defined resistance (2,742), a move placing major support (2,673) under siege.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -1.82% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P is traversing a wide range, capped by resistance matching the May peak (2,742).
Tactically, notable support matches the 2017 close (2,673) and is followed by an inflection point at the October closing low (2,641).
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has pulled in to its range bottom.
The prevailing downturn punctuates a failed retest of near-term resistance (25,510) as well as the June peak, an area better illustrated on the daily chart.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite’s COMP, -1.70% November price action remains technical, and equally bearish.
Recall that Friday’s high (7,274) precisely matched major resistance, an area that capped the Nasdaq last week. This week’s downturn punctuates the latest failed retest from underneath.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq continues to whipsaw, pulling in aggressively from the November peak. Three downside inflection points stand out:
Support matching the 2017 peak (7,004). The October low (6,922). Support matching the 2017 close (6,903). Beyond technical levels, the Nasdaq’s intermediate- to longer-term bias remains comfortably bearish, pending repairs.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow industrials’ backdrop is equally volatile.
Recall that notable support broadly spans from 24,719 to 24,876, levels matching the 2017 close and 2017 peak. Last week’s low (24,787) registered within the band.
Delving deeper, the October closing low (24,442) is followed by the absolute October low (24,122).
Separately, consider that Monday’s close marked the Dow’s second November close under the 200-day moving average, currently 25,096. The index is traversing less-charted territory against a bearish backdrop.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has pulled in sharply from the range top.
Recall that the November peak (2,815) registered two points under the mid-October peak.
The subsequent downturn places the S&P under the 200-day moving average (2,761) and the May peak (2,742) a familiar sticking point.
The bigger picture Collectively, the late-year market backdrop remains jagged and firmly bearish.
Broadly speaking, the recent market downdrafts have registered as aggressive, and powerful in spots, while the intervening rally attempts remain comparably lackluster.
More immediately, this week’s leg lower originates from well-defined resistance, including Nasdaq 7,274 and S&P 2,742.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF’s backdrop remains incrementally weaker.
As illustrated, the small-cap benchmark has topped under the mid-October peak as it digests the late-year breakdown. Tactically, a near-term floor spans from about 148.10 to 148.50, and is followed by the October closing low (145.95).
Similarly, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400 is digesting the October breakdown.
Here again, the mid-cap benchmark has registered a “lower high” versus the mid-October peak against the backdrop of a slightly downward sloping 200-day moving average.
Separately, the small- and mid-cap benchmarks both signaled a death cross last week, also known as a bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover.
Looking elsewhere, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 continues to whipsaw amid a bearish backdrop.
Though still early, the chart illustrates a developing double top defined by the mid-October and November peaks. The bearish pattern would be resolved with a violation of the October low.
Tactically, gap support (268.12), detailed previously, closely matched Monday’s low (268.07).
Delving deeper, the October closing low (263.86) is followed by the absolute October low (259.85).
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has failed its latest technical test.
Recall that notable resistance rests at the May peak (2,742). This area matches the June gap (2,742.9), and before Tuesday, also defined the mid-point of the November range (2,742.9).
The S&P’s failed retest from underneath places major support under siege.
The specific area matches the 2017 close (2,673) a level that initially held at last week’s low (2,670). A closing violation would place the S&P 500 in negative year-to-date territory.
Delving deeper, the October closing low (2,641) is followed by the absolute October low (2,603).
Beyond specific levels, the S&P 500’s intermediate- to longer-term bias remains comfortably bearish pending repairs. The holiday-shortened week typically translates to decreased volume, and material trend shifts rarely occur without volume.

See also: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 nails major support.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
FAANG-fueled selling pressure (plus Nvidia) paces November downdraft Drilling down further, persistent FAANG-fueled selling pressure — the acronym describing Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix and Alphabet (formerly Google) — continues to pace the November downdraft. Quickly consider each component:
To start, Facebook, Inc. FB, +0.67% has confirmed its downtrend, reaching 21-month lows.
The shares have been pressured as the company sorts through business model adjustments due to regulatory concerns, and amid reports of executive-level tensions.
Technically, the breakdown point (140) pivots to resistance and is followed by the firmer trendline, circa 150. An eventual close higher would place the brakes on bearish momentum.
Pending such a move, a downside target continues to project to the 123.50 area, detailed previously.
Meanwhile, Amazon.com’s AMZN, -1.11% backdrop remains firmly bearish.
Late last month, the shares staged a strong-volume downdraft, knifing under the 200-day moving average. The ensuing rally attempt was fueled by decreased volume, and capped by the breakdown point, circa 1,755. Bearish price action.
More immediately, the prevailing downturn places six-month lows under siege. A closing violation of the October low (1530.42) would confirm Amazon’s primary downtrend.
Looking elsewhere, Apple, Inc.’s AAPL, -4.78% backdrop — profiled last week — continues to deteriorate.
As illustrated, the shares have registered five straight closes under the 200-day moving average, raising the flag to a primary trend shift. Put differently, last week’s lackluster rally attempt was capped by the 200-day, punctuating a failed retest from underneath.
Slightly more broadly, the prevailing downturn originates from a failed early-November retest of the breakdown point (210.10) from underneath. The consecutive failed technical tests signal a bearish technical bias, pending repairs.
Tactically, major resistance spans from 193.90 to 194.20 — levels matching the 200-day and the August breakout point — and a swift reversal higher would mark technical progress. Conversely, deeper support, circa 182.20, closely matches the June range bottom, detailed previously.
Moving to Netflix NFLX, -1.34% — the fourth of the five FAANG components — its backdrop remains firmly bearish.
Technically, the prevailing downturn has been punctuated by Monday’s 50-day/200-day moving average crossover, more succinctly known as a death cross. Though frequently a lagging indicator, the crossover indicates that the intermediate-term downtrend has overtaken the primary trend.
More broadly, the November downturn originates from a failed early-month retest of the 200-day moving average from underneath.
Tactically, major support rests at 271.20 — a level matching the March and October lows — and a violation opens the path to a downside projected target, circa 215. Conversely, a close atop gap resistance (313) would mark a step toward stabilization.
Similarly, Alphabet, Inc. GOOGL, +0.29% is trending lower amid the overhang of last week’s death cross, or 50-day/200-day moving average crossover.
The prevailing downturn originates from failed retests of the 50- and 200-day moving averages from underneath.
Tactically, resistance spans from about 1,137 to 1,144 — an area matching the October gap — and an eventual close higher would mark technical progress.
Concluding with one stray note, former market favorite Nvidia Corp. NVDA, +3.03% is a large-cap semiconductor name under severe pressure.
This final chart exemplifies a real broad-market concern.
Consider that Monday’s close (144.70) placed the shares almost precisely 50% under the record close (289.36) established Oct. 1. The shares have been cut in half across about seven weeks.
Moreover, the downturn accelerated with last week’s sharp gap lower after the company’s third-quarter results. That incremental damage on this order is still being inflicted seven weeks into the market carnage signals that bearish momentum is intact.
